# MIDI BPM Detection v0.2.0

This release moves the plugin framework from the maintenance-mode NIH-plug
repository to its active nice-plug successor on Codeberg. The project and its
reusable parameter adapters now use nice-plug terminology throughout.

The shared downstream fork retains two capabilities used across the
maintainer's plugins: mutable background-task executors and a three-byte raw
MIDI escape hatch for sample-accurate control data routed through Bitwig's
normal MIDI/device graph.

The release provides:

- Separate CLAP and VST3 plugin packages for macOS arm64, macOS x86_64,
  Windows x86_64, and Linux x86_64.
- Desktop packages for macOS arm64, macOS x86_64, and Linux x86_64.
- The optional Bitwig controller extension used by the tempo-control
  integration.
- Generated third-party notices and checksums for the complete artifact set.

CLAP and VST3 are built and packaged separately. There is no Windows desktop
artifact, installer, universal macOS binary, or combined CLAP/VST3 archive.

## Build and runtime confidence

GitHub Actions builds the complete matrix, checks format-specific builds and
exports, packages notices, and verifies the thirteen-file asset set and
checksums. Successful automation is build and packaging evidence; it is not
runtime testing on each target platform.

Maintainer runtime experience is limited to macOS arm64. This note does not
claim that a specific plugin format and host combination was tested against
the final release candidate unless that claim is added during draft review.
macOS x86_64, Windows x86_64, and Linux x86_64 remain unverified at runtime.
Linux desktop is experimental.

macOS artifacts are unsigned and not notarized. Windows artifacts are
unsigned. No signing or notarization is provided for this release.

## VST3 licensing change

This release no longer uses the GPL-licensed `vst3-sys` binding from the
NIH-plug-era dependency graph. Nice-plug uses `vst3 0.3.0`, whose generated
bindings identify the MIT-licensed VST 3.8 SDK and are offered under
`MIT OR Apache-2.0`. The project source remains MIT. In addition to their
generated third-party notices, VST3 archives preserve Steinberg's VST 3.8 MIT
copyright and permission notice.

The former GPL-specific notice and corresponding-source release asset are no
longer required and are not part of `v0.2.0`. CLAP and VST3 remain separate
feature builds so each archive contains only its selected plugin format.

The Bitwig controller extension is optional and supports only the
tempo-control integration.
